projects.question: Can you tell me about your portfolio automation project?
projects.answer: One of my most advanced projects is my portfolio automation system. Users can trigger real automation tests directly from the UI. The system uses AWS Lambda to trigger GitHub Actions pipelines, which execute Playwright tests inside a Kubernetes-based environment. The results are then returned and displayed to the user. This project demonstrates my ability to build end-to-end automation infrastructure, combining frontend, backend, DevOps, and cloud technologies.

projects.question: What is your Live Logs project?
projects.answer: The Live Logs project is a real-time log streaming system that allows users to view logs directly from AWS EC2 instances. The application connects to remote servers and streams logs live to the user’s machine. It dynamically adapts to the user’s operating system by executing commands through Terminal (Unix-based) or CMD (Windows). The system is wrapped in a desktop application built with Electron.js, providing a seamless developer experience. This project demonstrates my ability to work with low-level system operations, cross-platform environments, and real-time data streaming.
projects.challenge: Handled cross-platform differences between Windows and Unix-based systems while maintaining a unified interface for log streaming.
projects.impact: Enabled developers to access and debug logs from remote servers in real time without manual SSH sessions, significantly improving troubleshooting efficiency.
